facts.fact: TheNigeriaLawyer reports that the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, led by Commissioner and CEO Dr Vincent Olatunji, is the statutory authority regulating data privacy and is acting.

NDPC chief Olatunji said the commission had investigated more than 240 breach cases, issued over 20 major remediation orders and named more than 1,900 non-compliant organisations in public notices, over about three years.
NJI Administrator Justice Adejumo described the Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 as a vital legal framework in use, and the NDPC chief cited its section 50 on judicial review of Commission orders.
TheNigeriaLawyer reports the Nigeria Data Protection Commission under CEO Dr Vincent Olatunji acting as the statutory regulator.

NDPC chief Olatunji said the commission had issued over 20 major remediation orders, investigated more than 240 breach cases and named more than 1,900 non-compliant organisations, over about three years.
The Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 is described by NJI Administrator Justice Adejumo as a vital legal framework for protecting personal data in the country.
Dr Vincent Olatunji speaks as Commissioner and CEO of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, described as the statutory authority.
NDPC chief Olatunji said more than 41,000 data controllers and processors of major importance registered within three years and over 8,000 compliance audit returns were received.
NDPC chief Olatunji said the commission had issued over 20 major remediation orders and named more than 1,900 non-compliant organisations in public notices, a count it publishes of its rulings.

NGA.note: The Malabo Convention and ECOWAS Act are cited only as norms the commission is mindful of; no signature, ratification or national law giving effect is stated.

facts.fact: NDPC chief Olatunji said Nigeria chairs the Regulatory Harmonisation Committee of the Network of African Data Protection Authorities.
